WHY NOBODY HAD EVER MEASURED §B, and it is not laziness. InputPipeline.latchForStep fires a scripted event when `e.f + scriptBase === sim.frame`. Out of combat a menu PAUSES the world, Engine._step() returns before stepOnce(), and sim.frame FREEZES — so only `f: 0` can ever match and every event at f>=1 waits for a frame that never comes. A page turn needs two frames (the axis is edge-detected), so out of combat it needs a frame that does not exist. PROVED in the browser, not argued: with the world paused, the f:0 turn LANDS and the f:1 turn does NOT, and the frame counter moved 0. This is a HARNESS limit, not a player-visible defect (RealInput writes moveX straight into the pipeline, unkeyed), but it blocks scripted measurement of EVERY menu that pauses. §B is therefore driven in combat, where the clock runs — a shipped, specified configuration, because T6 says in as many words that reading in a fight is permitted.

THE FIRST CUT OF MY OWN PROBE WAS WRONG TWICE, both times in the UNIT. getUIState().book.page is a 1-based PAGE number (focus.book.page * 2 + 1); a spread is two pages (§A B6's preferred Morrowind form), so one input moving the reported page by 2 is T2 SATISFIED. And T4 read 2-instead-of-4 only because the clamp I had just landed was correctly holding the book at its last spread — the T4 fixture had no room to turn. Rewinding first fixed it.
